name: GTFire
iocPatterns: Phishing sites hosted on Firebase subdomains such as *.firebaseapp.com or *.web.app
Large volume of randomly generated domains with short‑life registrations
Encoded URLs embedded within translate.goog redirect chains
IDN punycode domains used for phishing pages
Double‑encoded Base64 query strings in malicious URLs
keyCapabilities: Uses Google Firebase hosting infrastructure to deploy phishing web pages at scale
Registers large volumes of random *.web.app subdomains
Abuses Google Translate translation proxy as a URL disguise layer
Chains multiple redirects to obfuscate the final malicious destination
Reuses brand‑specific login templates across different targets
Collects credentials through multi‑step form processing and extracts them via HTTP GET
Centralizes harvested data on organized C2 servers
Employs IDN Punycode encoding with occasional double‑encoding of Base64 parameters
Exfiltrates passwords in Base64 format within URL parameters
Attaches telemetry data such as country and browser language to requests
Relies on commercial All-in-1 PHP phishing scripts for rapid deployment
Runs behind LiteSpeed Web Server to reduce detection risk
recommendedActions: Monitor and block suspicious .web.app subdomains that host phishing content
Inspect traffic involving Google Translate domains (translate.goog) for unusual redirects or multi‑step chains
Implement advanced URL filtering that analyzes redirect paths rather than solely relying on reputation scores
Provide user awareness training focused on spearphishing links disguised via translation proxies
Enforce multi‑factor authentication to mitigate credential compromise
Audit outbound HTTP GET requests carrying credential data for anomalies and telemetry

campaignsText: GTFire has demonstrated the ability to compromise over 1,000 organizations spanning more than 100 countries, exploiting a variety of sectors such as government, finance, manufacturing, defense, and education. The actor’s operational tempo is rapid, enabled by automated deployment tools that create thousands of phishing pages in minutes. Their campaign relies on legitimizing infrastructure—Google services—to bypass conventional URL reputation engines, employing elaborate redirect chains, encoded parameters, and dynamic domain registration to maintain persistence in the wild.
description: GTFire is a financially motivated threat actor that exploits legitimate Google services—Firebase hosting and Translate redirects—to launch large‑scale phishing campaigns across more than 100 countries. By auto‑generating thousands of subdomains, chaining multiple redirects, and exfiltrating credentials via HTTP GET requests, they evade traditional reputation filters with minimal operational overhead.
goals: GTFire’s strategic objective is to acquire monetary value through rapid credential theft. Their broad sector focus—including government, finance, manufacturing, defense, and education—reflects an opportunistic approach, harvesting credentials for immediate resale or potential lateral movement. The actor targets a global audience, employing highly generic spear‑phishing tactics designed to bypass reputation and traditional security controls.
